title: The point space of a qcqs algebraic space is spectral
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Give its field-valued point classes $|X|$ the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that every open covering of $|X|$ has a finite subcover and that the absolute diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is quasi-compact, meaning that its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact point space. Then $|X|$ is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]: it is quasi-compact, every nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point, quasi-compact open subsets form a basis, and the intersection of two quasi-compact open subsets is quasi-compact. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The assumed absolute diagonal is quasi-compact by the affine-test and representable-map equivalences of [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Its base change along $X\times_S X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is the relative diagonal $X\to X\times_S X$: on every scheme test both pullbacks impose equality of the same two maps to $X$. Quasi-compactness survives this base change by the same cited statement. Thus the relative-diagonal hypothesis of [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] holds, and that lemma gives a unique generic point for each nonempty irreducible closed subset of $|X|$.

source.place: Tag 0A4G, first two sentences; Tag 06NJ (lemma-quasi-separated-sober); Tags 03HF and 03HD for the relative-diagonal test.

proof.text: Choose an affine scheme $U$ and a representable surjective etale map $p:U\to X$ using [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]; the quotient topology in that statement is precisely the atlas topology here by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. For each affine open $V\subseteq U$, let $B_V=|p|(|V|)$. The restricted map $V\to X$ is representable etale: on every scheme test its pullback is the restriction to an open subscheme of the etale scheme map testing $p$, hence etale by parts (1) and (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Therefore $B_V$ is open and $|V|\to|X|$ is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so $B_V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact]. For any open $O\subseteq|X|$ and $x\in O$, lift $x$ to $u\in U$. Continuity makes $|p|^{-1}(O)$ open; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] gives an affine open $u\in V\subseteq|p|^{-1}(O)$. Hence $x\in B_V\subseteq O$, proving that these quasi-compact opens form a basis.

source.place: Tag 0A4G, affine-atlas and quasi-compact-open-basis paragraph; Tags 03H6, 03BX, 01IT, 04Z9.

proof.text: Let $A,B\subseteq|X|$ be quasi-compact open subsets. Cover each by the basis opens from step 2 contained in it; quasi-compactness gives finite expressions $A=\bigcup_i B_{V_i}$ and $B=\bigcup_j B_{W_j}$ with $V_i,W_j$ affine opens of $U$. Each $V_i\to X$ is a quasi-compact morphism by [lem-sfb-space-affine-source-qc-separated], using exactly the absolute quasi-separatedness assumed here. Consequently its pullback along the affine scheme $W_j\to X$ is a quasi-compact scheme $V_i\times_XW_j$. By [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], every pair of points of $V_i,W_j$ with equal image in $|X|$ lifts to this fibre product. It follows, in both inclusions, that the image of $|V_i\times_XW_j|\to|X|$ is $B_{V_i}\cap B_{W_j}$. This point map is continuous by the same cited node, so [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact] makes this intersection quasi-compact. Finally $A\cap B=\bigcup_{i,j}(B_{V_i}\cap B_{W_j})$ is quasi-compact: an open cover restricts to each of the finitely many quasi-compact pieces; combine their finite subcovers. Empty index sets give the empty intersection case automatically.

source.place: Tag 0A4G, final intersection paragraph, with finite affine chart images in place of affine covers of the two open subspaces; Tag 0AHR (lemma-characterize-quasi-separated).

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of $|X|$ is the first hypothesis. Step 1 gives sobriety, step 2 a basis of quasi-compact opens, and step 3 the intersection property. These are exactly the four conditions in [def-weil-spectral-space]. Therefore $|X|$ is spectral.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0A4G (lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral), with its affine-chart intersection argument written using finite covers by images of affine opens.

With the affine-test and representable equivalence in lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests, this gives the hypothesis of lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober, whose conclusion includes uniqueness of the generic point. Step 2: lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas needs only that |X| is quasi-compact. Each affine open V of the atlas U maps to X by a representable étale map (open immersion composed with étale). The images |p|(|V|) are open, quasi-compact and form a basis, by the point-open calculus, 04Z9 and 01IT. No qc open of U is assumed to be affine. Step 3: lem-sfb-space-affine-source-qc-separated (08IL) applies to the étale map V_i→X with X absolutely quasi-separated, so V_i×_X W_j is a quasi-compact scheme. Surjectivity onto the fibre product of point sets (03H4) makes its image exactly B_{V_i}∩B_{W_j}, and finite unions of these are quasi-compact. Step 4 matches the four conditions of def-weil-spectral-space. Edge cases checked: empty X, empty A or B, a point, and a non-separated base S.
